recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Expand and divide by √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply the bracket out first so the coefficients are visible, then divide by √(a²+b²) — which is 2 again, since (√2)² + (√2)² = 4.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply the bracket out FIRST so the coefficients show, then divide by √((√2)² + (√2)²) = 2.

recall.must_convey: That the bracket is expanded and both sides divided by 2, giving coefficients of 1/√2.

steps.why: Leaving the √2 outside the bracket hides the coefficients. Expanding first is what lets √(a²+b²) be computed at all.
common_mistakes: Dividing by √2 because it is outside the bracket.

steps.label: Recognise the standard angles
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 1/√2 is BOTH cos45° and sin45°, so this pattern is cosA cosB + sinA sinB — the cos(A−B) form, not a sine one.
steps.memory_tip: 1/√2 is both cos 45° and sin 45°, so this is the cosA cosB + sinA sinB pattern, not a sine one.

recall.must_convey: That 1/√2 is read as cos45° and sin45°, and √3/2 as cos30° — matching the cos(A−B) pattern.

steps.why: Equal coefficients always land on 45°, because that is the one angle whose sine and cosine are the same. That is why this twin gives a cosine equation where the other gave a sine.
common_mistakes: Reading √3/2 as sin60° and finishing with a sine equation.

steps.label: Collapse to one function
steps.margin_note: Third mark. cosA cosB + sinA sinB is cos(A−B). The principal value is π/6.
steps.memory_tip: cosA cosB + sinA sinB = cos(A − B), so the angle is x − π/4. The principal value is π/6.

recall.must_convey: That the equation becomes cos(x − π/4) = cos(π/6) with principal value π/6.

steps.why: A cosine equation and a sine equation have DIFFERENT general solutions, so which function the left side collapses into decides the last line entirely.
common_mistakes: Taking the principal value as π/4.

steps.label: Write the general solution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. For a COSINE equation the general solution is 2nπ ± α — note the ± and the 2n, both different from the sine form.
steps.memory_tip: For a COSINE equation it is 2nπ ± α — the ± and the 2n both differ from the sine form. Add the π/4 back.

steps.why: Cosine is even, so both +α and −α satisfy the equation — which is why its general solution carries a ± where the sine form carries (−1)ⁿ.
common_mistakes: Using nπ + (−1)ⁿα for a cosine equation.

insider_note: Divide by √(a² + b²) = 2, not by √2, so the right side becomes √3/2. It then collapses to cos(x − π/4) = cos(π/6), and the cosine general solution 2nπ ± α is the one to use.
